Welcome to Uffington Church of England Primary School.
At Uffington C of E Primary School, we pride ourselves on being an inclusive school that caters to children aged 3 to 11. We believe that every child deserves an exceptional education and strive to create an environment where everyone feels valued and supported.
Situated at the heart of the community, our school is nestled close to the beautiful White Horse Hill. This picturesque location provides a serene backdrop for our students to learn and grow.
With four classes spanning from Pre-School to Year 6, we offer a nurturing and stimulating learning environment. Our dedicated and passionate staff are committed to providing high-quality education that meets the needs of each individual child.
We are proud to be a good school with outstanding elements. This achievement is a testament to the hard work and dedication of our staff, students, governors and parents. We continuously strive for excellence and are constantly seeking ways to improve and enhance our provision.
At Uffington C of E Primary School, our core Christian values of love, respect, resilience, and our theologically routed vision 'Everyone Matters' are at the heart of everything we do. We believe that by instilling this vision and values in our students, we are equipping them with the tools they need to become compassionate, confident, and responsible individuals.
We recognise that education is not solely about academic achievement. Therefore, we focus on the whole child, nurturing their social, emotional, and physical well-being. Our holistic approach ensures that each child receives a well-rounded education that prepares them for success in all aspects of life.
We would love to welcome you to our school and share our learning journey with you. Whether you are a prospective parent, community member, or visitor, we invite you to explore our website, attend our events, and witness the incredible learning experiences taking place at Uffington C of E Primary School.

pageCache.text:
Breakfast Club
Our Breakfast club takes place every day during term time from 7.45am to the start of the school day. The sessions are run in the school hall and children should be dropped off by a responsible adult to breakfast club staff via the brown door in the main playground.Who runs breakfast club?The breakfast club is run by Miss Whitehorn who is a very experienced member of the school staff team.Why should I send my child to breakfast club?A healthy breakfast is just the start for your child when they spend time in breakfast club. As well as the peace of mind of knowing your child is well cared for, the sessions offer children a huge range of activities to get involved in for example junk modelling and outdoor games, as well as social time with other children. Please click on the link to view the breakfast club welcome pack. All in all, a really great start to the school day!How do I register my child for breakfast club?Welcome packs are available here, or from the school office.Once you are registered with our club you will be able to book your sessions in advance online via your MCAS (MyChildAtSchool) account. Parent guidance here.How much does breakfast club cost?We provide a number of flexible options for our Breakfast club:Option 1 - £6.00 a session (from 7.45 am to school start time includes breakfast).Option 2 - £5.00 (from 7.45 am to school start time - no breakfast)Option 3 - £3.00 (from 8.30 am to school start time - no breakfast)Option 4 - £4.00 (for taxi children - includes breakfast)These costs are in-line with other similar childcare providers in the local area. Some families can receive assistance with breakfast club charges via the tax-free childcare voucher scheme. For more information on this, please click here to view the breakfast club welcome pack.If you require any further information please contact the school office on 01367 820296 or email: office@uffingtonprimary.org

pageCache.text:
Supporting Young Carers
At Uffington Church of England Primary School, we recognise the vital role young carers play within their families and our community. We are committed to supporting our young carers to ensure their wellbeing, educational success, and personal development.
What is a Young Carer?
A young carer is someone under 18 who helps care for a family member who has:
A physical or mental illness
A problem with alcohol or drugs
Other health-related needs
Young carers might help with tasks like cooking, cleaning, shopping, giving medicine, or offering emotional support.
Partnership with Be Free Young Carers
We are proud to work closely with Be Free Young Carers, a charity dedicated to supporting young carers in our local area. Through this partnership, we provide tailored support and access to resources that help young carers balance their caring responsibilities with school life.
Be Free Young Carers
Young Carers Register
To ensure we identify and support all young carers in our school community, we maintain a Young Carers Register. This confidential register helps us monitor the wellbeing and progress of young carers and ensures they receive the appropriate support.
If you believe your child is a young carer or if your child would like to register, please contact us or speak directly with our Young Carers Lead.
Young Carers Lead
Our designated Young Carers Lead is Mrs Helen Reade (HLTA). Helen is available to provide support, guidance, and a listening ear for young carers. She works closely with Be Free Young Carers and other professionals to ensure our young carers have the help they need to thrive.
You can contact Mrs Reade via the school office.
Support and Resources
Emotional and practical support within school.
Confidentiality and Respect
We understand that being a young carer can sometimes be challenging and personal. All information shared with the Young Carers Lead is treated with the utmost respect.

G said," I enjoyed it all. The cookie making and snail race. B gave me part of his prize."

Our Governors
We are a carefully selected group of people, chosen or elected to represent a cross section of skills and experience. We access local training to ensure the knowledge base of the governing body is suitable, and regularly monitor this to ensure we remain as such. This brings us together as a diverse and varied team, enabling us to look at issues from multiple perspectives. The governing body always includes the Head teacher and a member of staff from the school.
Our primary purpose is not the day-to-day operations of the school, that is the role of the Head teacher. The governing body is here to work alongside her, to set the long term strategy and financial plan for the school, steer academic performance and support the Head teacher to deliver and ensure compliance with local and national policy.
Our governors all belong to one of two committees which encompass the work of the governing body. They also work alongside a member of staff to support our School Development Plan.

Remote Learning Plan
To ensure that learning continues uninterrupted, regardless of school closures, restrictions on attendance, or individual cases where a pupil is unable to attend school but is still able to learn, Uffington C of E Primary School has developed the following remote learning plan. This plan provides opportunities for remote learning while also recognising that some households may have limited or no access to devices and may require hard copies of work and resources.
This plan will be implemented in the following circumstances:
School Closures or Attendance RestrictionsWhen access to the school is restricted for pupils due to closures or government guidelines.
Individual Cases of AbsenceWhen a pupil is unable to attend school for personal reasons but is still capable of engaging in learning activities.
This plan is designed to comply with the expectations and principles set out by the Department for Education (DfE).

Sports Premium
We work with Elite Youth Sports to help teach our PE curriculum, extra-curricular lunchtime and after school clubs. Elite Youth Sports are a professional sports coaching company that help primary schools to enhance their Physical Education by providing external sports coaches.
Having them on board has helped us to increase the range of sports offered and allowed us to make our lessons more inclusive. We ensure that everyone is included and encouraged to engage in a wide and varied Physical Education (PE) programme.
